title: What If a City Turned a Whole River Backward? Chicago Did
subject: Chicago River

scenes.text: What if a city turned a river backward? In 1900, Chicago did.
Chicago's sewage flowed down the Chicago River into Lake Michigan, the same lake the city drank from.
That helped spread typhoid and other waterborne disease, so the river had to flow somewhere else.
Starting in 1892, workers dug a canal roughly thirty miles long, cutting through hills to reach the Des Plaines River.
Tens of millions of cubic yards of earth and rock were removed over eight years.
On January 2, 1900, workers broke the last dam, and the river began flowing away from the lake, toward the Mississippi. It has flowed backward ever since.

description:
What if a city turned a river backward?
Chicago dug a canal and reversed its river in 1900 to keep sewage out of its drinking water.
